We're looking for an experienced Affiliate Partnerships Executive to join us on a 6-month contract and grow our affiliate channel across Europe and the Middle East.

• Build and own the affiliate growth plan for Europe and the Middle East, identifying priority markets, partner types and targets.

• Negotiate and agree commercial terms in line with our CAC and payback targets.
• Manage and develop partner relationships, optimising placements, offers and creative to maximise new customers and first trades.
• Report on partner and channel performance against CAC and first trade targets, making clear recommendations on where to invest and where to stop.
• Work with Compliance to ensure all partners and promotions meet regulatory requirements, including approving partner content and monitoring activity.
• Monitor traffic quality and protect IG against fraud and poor-quality activity.
• Work with Marketing, Creative and Product to adapt assets, offers and messaging for local markets.
• Test new partner models and opportunities, and scale what works.
• Document your learnings and build clear playbooks so the channel can keep growing beyond your contract.
• Use AI to work faster, from partner research to reporting. Curiosity with AI is a must.
What success looks like
• A strong pipeline of new partners signed and live across priority markets
• Demonstrable growth in new customers and first trades from Europe and the Middle East
• Performance at or below our CAC and payback targets
• Compliant, high-quality partner activity with robust monitoring in place
• A clear playbook and a business case showing the value of making the role permanent

What You'll Need:
• Proven experience in affiliate or partnership marketing, with a track record of recruiting partners and growing the channel
• Strong commercial and negotiation skills, comfortable agreeing performance-based deals such as CPA and revenue share
• Experience managing partners through affiliate networks and tracking platforms
• A data-led approach, with the ability to analyse performance and optimise against acquisition cost
• Experience working across international markets, ideally in Europe and the Middle East, with an understanding of local market differences
• Strong stakeholder management and the ability to work independently and at pace
• Strong eye for detail, especially around compliance and partner quality
• Curiosity about AI and how it can improve how we work
Ideally you will also have

•

Compensation details will be shared by the recruiter during the first interview.

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. About the role:

This role owns the product direction, roadmap and outcomes for Performance Engineering and Quality Engineering within Infrastructure & Operations. You will shape shared capabilities that help engineering teams test earlier, detect risk sooner and release reliable, performant software with confidence.
You will work at the intersection of specialist performance and quality engineers, software delivery teams, platform engineers and technology leadership. The role combines strong product management with sufficient technical depth to understand how automated testing, non-functional testing and quality controls integrate with CI/CD pipelines and the wider software delivery lifecycle.

Your role in the Team’s Success:

Performance Engineering builds reusable components for performance testing and acceptance environments, including pipeline integrations, load generation, mocking, ephemeral environments and observability. Quality Engineering provides scalable test solutions, quality tooling, engineering metrics, contract testing, acceptance testing and synthetic monitoring.
Your focus is to turn these capabilities into accessible, measurable internal products that solve real engineering problems. You will bridge the needs of platform builders and consuming teams, while engineering leads retain ownership of technical design and day-to-day delivery.

What you’ll do:

• Define and own a coherent product strategy and prioritised roadmap across Performance Engineering and Quality Engineering.
• Position performance and quality capabilities as internal products, with clear users, problems, propositions, service boundaries and measurable outcomes.
• Balance strategic investment, reliability improvements, adoption work and emerging engineering requirements using evidence and agreed prioritisation principles.
• Connect the roadmap to broader engineering goals, including faster feedback, safer releases, improved delivery performance and reduced production risk.

Discovery & stakeholder engagement

• Run structured discovery with software engineers, quality engineers, performance engineers, platform teams and engineering leaders to identify high-value problems.
• Translate user needs, delivery constraints and technical risks into clear product requirements, outcomes and prioritised backlog items.
• Partner with engineering leads and architects to validate feasibility, understand trade-offs and sequence work without prescribing the technical solution.
• Build alignment across stakeholders, communicate decisions clearly and maintain transparency on product direction, progress, dependencies and risks.

Delivery, backlog & planning

• Own planning and backlog management, ensuring initiatives, features and epics are outcome-led, well defined and ready for engineering delivery.
• Work closely with engineering teams to manage scope, dependencies, trade-offs and release priorities, while engineering leads own execution and technical delivery.
• Define acceptance criteria and success measures before delivery, and use evidence after release to decide whether to iterate, scale or stop.
• Maintain an actionable roadmap and provide concise, evidence-based updates to senior technology stakeholders.

Adoption & continuous improvement

• Define adoption strategies for shared testing frameworks, pipeline components, quality standards, performance tooling and engineering insights.
• Reduce friction for consuming teams through clear onboarding paths, enablement, reusable patterns and effective feedback loops.
• Monitor adoption, product health and engineering outcomes, using qualitative and quantitative evidence to improve the product continuously.
• Promote shift-left quality and performance practices so that risks are identified during design and delivery rather than after release.

What you’ll need:

• Hands-on background as an automated test engineer, SDET, quality engineer or closely related technical role, with strong understanding of test automation and modern software delivery.
• Practical understanding of how quality functions integrate with CI/CD pipelines, including automated checks, quality gates, test stages, reporting and feedback loops.
• Experience with non-functional testing, particularly performance, load, stress, scalability, reliability or resilience testing.
• Product management or delivery leadership experience covering product planning, discovery, roadmap and backlog management, stakeholder alignment and delivery prioritisation.
• Ability to translate complex engineering problems into clear product outcomes, requirements, acceptance criteria and success measures.
• Good understanding of the software development lifecycle, DevOps practices, cloud platforms, APIs, observability and modern testing approaches.
• Credibility with engineers: able to discuss architecture, tooling choices, test strategy and delivery-pipeline trade-offs without needing to design or code the solution.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to align specialist teams, platform users and senior technology leaders.
• Comfortable using data to prioritise investment and measure impact, while recognising where qualitative discovery is needed.
• Experience driving adoption or behavioural change across engineering teams in a matrix or distributed organisation.

Desirable
• Experience productising shared test automation frameworks, developer tooling, engineering platforms or internal enablement services.
• Familiarity with contract testing, mocking, synthetic monitoring, ephemeral test environments and acceptance testing.
• Familiarity with performance-testing tools such as k6, Gatling or Locust, and with interpreting performance results and regressions.
• Exposure to engineering metrics such as DORA, defect trends, test coverage, escaped defects, pipeline pass rates or service-level indicators.
• Experience with GitLab or similar CI/CD platforms, cloud environments, infrastructure as code, containers and observability tooling.
• Experience in a regulated industry such as financial services or fintech.

What success looks like

Success measures will be baselined and agreed with engineering leadership. They are expected to include:
• Performance and quality capabilities are represented through a clear, current and trusted roadmap.
• Priority services have defined non-functional requirements and meaningful performance baselines.
• Performance and quality checks are embedded earlier in delivery pipelines, with regressions and defects detected before production.
• Adoption of supported automation frameworks, pipeline components, synthetic monitoring and testing patterns increases across engineering teams.
• Friction to onboard and use shared capabilities reduces, supported by measurable user feedback.
• Engineering leaders have clearer visibility of quality, delivery and performance risks through agreed metrics and insights.
• Backlog and investment decisions are traceable to user problems, strategic priorities and measurable outcomes.

What this role does not own

• Day-to-day delivery management of the Performance Engineering or Quality Engineering teams, which remains with engineering leadership.

About the Opportunity

As OKX US continues to grow, we are looking for a Support Operations Lead to join our Business Management team, with a focus on leading and coaching our global Customer Support (CS) function to better serve OKX users. Rather than being a direct member of the CS team, you’ll work alongside Operations, Compliance, Product, and Marketing stakeholders to uplift the quality, efficiency, and regulatory compliance of our offshore CS agents.

You’ll act as a subject matter expert (SME) for all things within the customer support experience — helping offshore agents understand local customer expectations, regulations, and how to handle issues with care and accuracy. This is a strategic and high-impact role, laying the groundwork for improved CS experience and potentially a local team in the future.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Represent the voice of the customer within the business and act as SME for support needs, regulations, and expectations.

•

Coach and guide offshore CS teams to improve handling of tickets, especially regulatory-sensitive cases (e.g., scam/fraud, ID verification).

•

Partner with local Compliance, Operations, and Legal to ensure offshore CS agents are trained and updated on local regulatory requirements.

•

Manage high-priority and escalated customer cases in collaboration with offshore agents and local teams.

•

Liaise with Customer Due Diligence (CDD) teams to improve KYC/AML workflows for customers and reduce customer friction.

•

Act as SME for OKX Card support operations — guiding offshore CS on dispute handling, chargeback processes, and cardholder issue resolution in line with card program compliance requirements.

•

Work closely with Product and Marketing teams to proactively inform CS of upcoming campaigns, changes, or product launches that may drive ticket volume.

•

Identify operational pain points in the customer journey and work cross-functionally to resolve or escalate them.

•

Develop SOPs, quick guides, and training materials to help offshore agents respond more effectively to users.

•

Track key CS metrics such as resolution time, CSAT, and escalation volume to measure success and identify improvement areas.

•

If the business moves toward a local CS team in the future, help scope, plan, and build this function from the ground up.

What We Look For In You

Experience & Industry Knowledge

•

5+ years of experience in customer operations, customer experience, or support leadership, ideally within fintech, crypto, or financial services.

•

Solid understanding of US financial regulation, consumer protection expectations, and AML/KYC processes.

•

Experience working with or leading offshore support teams in a high-growth or regulated environment.

•

Exposure to customer-centric operations functions — blending support, risk, compliance, and product feedback loops.

Skills & Competencies

•

Strong leadership and coaching ability, with a focus on raising offshore team performance without direct line management.

•

Excellent stakeholder management skills — ability to work across compliance, product, marketing, and support teams.

•

Operationally minded — you're a problem-solver who can turn user pain points into action plans.

•

Process-driven — capable of designing and implementing SOPs and knowledge base content.

•

Excellent communicator — able to distill regulatory complexity into practical CS guidance.

•

Analytical — confident using data and KPIs to improve customer outcomes and support operations.

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

•

L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development

•

Various team building programs and company events

•

Wellness and meal allowances

•

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

Envie de transformer votre intérêt pour les marchés financiers en expérience concrète ?

Si vous êtes curieux(se) des marchés, du trading et de l’investissement, que vous aimez le contact humain et souhaitez apprendre dans un environnement international, ce stage pourrait être fait pour vous.
En tant que Sales Intern chez Saxo, vous rejoindrez notre équipe Sales à Paris et bénéficierez d’une expérience concrète au contact des clients, des marchés financiers et de nos solutions de trading et d’investissement.

Vos missions
• Accompagner l’équipe Sales dans la gestion des leads et la conversion de prospects en clients.
• Participer à l’onboarding de nouveaux clients et les accompagner dans la découverte de nos plateformes, produits et services.
• Contribuer au processus d’ouverture de comptes et aux tâches administratives associées.
• Participer aux initiatives commerciales et aux actions destinées à nos clients.
• Préparer des notes de marché et de recherche à destination des clients.
• Travailler aux côtés de Sales expérimentés et développer vos connaissances des marchés financiers et de l’investissement.

Le profil que nous recherchons
Nous recherchons avant tout une personne énergique, curieuse et proactive. Vous n’avez pas besoin de tout savoir dès le premier jour, mais vous devez avoir envie d’apprendre, de prendre des initiatives et de vous investir.

Vous êtes :
• Étudiant(e) ou jeune diplômé(e) d’une école de commerce ou d’une université, idéalement avec une spécialisation en finance, marchés financiers ou dans un domaine similaire.
• Réellement intéressé(e) par le trading, l’investissement et les marchés financiers.
• Proactif(ve) et à l’aise avec l’idée de prendre des initiatives.
• Énergique, ambitieux(se) et motivé(e) par les résultats.
• À l’aise dans les échanges et aimez créer du contact avec des profils variés.
• Capable de travailler en équipe tout en prenant la responsabilité de vos propres missions.
• Curieux(se), adaptable et à l’aise dans un environnement international qui évolue rapidement.
• À l’aise en français comme en anglais.

Pourquoi rejoindre Saxo ?
Chez Saxo, vous serez entouré(e) de personnes passionnées par les marchés, la technologie et les nouvelles façons d’investir.
Vous aurez l’opportunité d’apprendre auprès de collègues expérimentés, de contribuer à de véritables activités commerciales et de découvrir de l’intérieur le fonctionnement d’un acteur international du trading et de l’investissement.

Nous pensons que les bonnes idées peuvent venir de partout. Même en tant que stagiaire, nous voulons que vous posiez des questions, apportiez votre point de vue, challengiez les idées et preniez des initiatives.

Vous rejoindrez un environnement international où des collaborateurs aux parcours et cultures variés travaillent ensemble, avec une vraie place accordée au feedback, au développement et à la collaboration.
Apportez votre curiosité, votre énergie et votre intérêt pour les marchés. Nous vous donnerons l’opportunité de les mettre en action.

Prêt(e) à nous rejoindre?
Envoyez-nous votre CV accompagné de quelques lignes expliquant pourquoi la vente, les marchés financiers et Saxo vous intéressent.
Veuillez noter que l’anglais est la langue de travail chez Saxo et qu’une partie du processus de recrutement pourra donc se dérouler en anglais.

Nous avons hâte de vous rencontrer!
Ce que j’ai ajusté : j’ai privilégié un français naturel pour une cible étudiante en France plutôt qu’une traduction littérale. Lorsque vous apportez passion, curiosité, dynamisme et esprit d'équipe, votre parcours d'apprentissage sera dynamique et vos opportunités de carrière chez Saxo seront immenses.

Chez Saxo, nous n'offrons pas seulement un emploi, nous offrons une opportunité d'investir dans votre avenir!

The Graphic Designer role will help bring the Topstep brand to life across a wide range of digital and marketing initiatives. This role is dedicated exclusively to the Prop Trading team, creating compelling visual experiences that attract, educate, and engage traders throughout every stage of their journey. From performance marketing campaigns and product launches to landing pages, email, social media, and lifecycle marketing, this designer will play a key role in strengthening the brand that powers Topstep's continued growth.

The ideal candidate is a highly creative, detail-oriented designer with 4 + years of professional experience and a strong foundation in branding, digital design, typography, and visual storytelling. They should be comfortable owning projects from concept through execution while collaborating with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Design compelling creative assets across digital, web, email, social, advertising, presentations, and other marketing channels.

• Execute creative concepts that align with campaign objectives, brand standards, and business goals.

• Help maintain and evolve the visual identity of Topstep by applying established brand guidelines consistently.

• Design landing pages, web graphics, templates, and other digital experiences in collaboration with UX, marketing, and development teams.

• Work closely with Art Directors, Project Managers, Copywriters, and other stakeholders to develop thoughtful creative solutions.

• Present design concepts and clearly communicate creative rationale while incorporating feedback throughout the design process.

• Contribute ideas during creative brainstorming sessions and campaign development.

Required Qualifications and Key Competencies

• Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communications, Advertising, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).

• 4 + years of experience as a graphic designer in an in-house creative team or agency environment.

• A strong portfolio showcasing exceptional branding, digital marketing, and visual design work across multiple channels.

• Expert understanding of typography, color, composition, layout, and visual storytelling.

Throughput - messages per second (orders + cancels) under exchange burst scenarios.

About the Company

Founded in Sydney in 2007, IC is a global trading brand built around precision and performance. We combine advanced trading technology with deep liquidity, low-latency connectivity and infrastructure designed for traders. Everything is built around execution, control and the needs of traders who treat trading as a craft.

The same standards shape how we work. Precision. Performance. Transparency. Respect. We value people who know their craft, take ownership and hold themselves to high standards. As IC grows globally, we are building teams that move with purpose and focus on what matters.

About the Job

We are looking for a Salesforce Developer who approaches Salesforce development through the lens of modern software engineering. At IC, Salesforce is where our sales, retention, partner and support teams work every day. We maintain a modular DX codebase, enforce clean object-oriented design patterns, build Lightning Web Components to a consistent design system, and follow strict code-quality and testing practices. If you enjoy writing clean, decoupled Apex, designing reactive and localised LWC frontends, and working in a modern Git and scratch-org workflow without legacy clutter, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll own

• Turn requirements into technical designs, then deliver Apex and Lightning Web Components for our support, sales, KYC, trading account, payment and partner workflows.

• Work with our trigger framework and Unit of Work, query builder, collection utilities, async actions and batch frameworks.

• Build reusable Lightning Web Components to our design system, with a custom label for every string and locale-aware formatting.

• Build and maintain REST integrations with payload validation, resilient error handling and mockable tests.

• Write bulkified, governor-aware code and async pipelines, and resolve performance bottlenecks and technical debt.

• Implement permission set groups, custom permissions, sharing and field-level security for every new feature.

• Write deterministic tests that check behaviour, not just coverage.

• Release through scratch orgs, pull requests and automated validation, from stage to UAT to production.

• Own features from design to production, delivering scalable, well-documented code to our engineering standards.

What you’ll need

Essential

• 3+ years of hands-on Salesforce development in an enterprise org.

• Strong Apex: triggers, Queueable, Batch and Scheduled jobs, bulkification and governor limits.

• Strong LWC and modern JavaScript (ES6+): lifecycle hooks, reactivity and component composition.

• Object-oriented design: SOLID principles and common design patterns.

• REST integrations: outbound callouts, inbound Apex REST, JSON, and Named and External Credentials.

• Solid SOQL skills: selective queries, indexing and safe dynamic query generation for large data volumes.

• Salesforce DX, sf CLI, Git, GitHub and a pull-request workflow.

• Salesforce Platform Developer I certification.

Your approach

• You read existing code before adding to it, and your changes look like they belong.

• You ask what problem a ticket solves before you estimate it, and flag gaps in a requirement early.

• You support your features after release and fix your own bugs first.

• You communicate clearly with developers, BAs and QA, including colleagues in other time zones.

• You’re keen to learn the trading domain: accounts, IBs, KYC and multi-entity regulation.

Desirable

• Salesforce Platform Developer II, or a Sales/Service Cloud Consultant certification

• Hands-on experience using Generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, or GitHub Copilot) for code generation, Apex/LWC refactoring, test class generation, and rapid debugging.

• Unlocked packages and package-based development

• Event-driven design with Platform Events

• Service Cloud experience, including CTI and call-centre integrations

About Busha

Since our inception in 2018, Busha has been at the forefront of digital currency exchange, offering trading options in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum. Our mission is to build an open financial system characterized by innovation, efficiency, and user-friendliness. We value Clear Communication, Positive Energy, Efficient Execution, and Continuous Learning in all our team members.

At Busha, we are building technology that makes financial services more accessible, efficient and reliable. Busha Pro is our spot exchange for crypto and fiat, where speed, reliability and security are essential to delivering a seamless trading experience for our users.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to work on the engineering behind a live exchange where speed, reliability and accuracy matter.

You will take ownership of and improve the systems responsible for processing orders, matching trades and supporting exchange operations: operating them in production, making them faster and extending them safely.

Overview

We are looking for someone who understands more than just writing code. You should understand how trading systems work, how to build them reliably at scale and how to solve the technical challenges that come with real-time transactions.

You will have meaningful ownership of technical decisions, shape the platform's architecture and work closely with the wider team to turn product requirements into reliable, production-ready systems.

Responsibilities

• Take ownership of the Busha Pro exchange: learn the codebase deeply, operate it in production and harden it.
• Design, build and optimize the backend systems that power Busha Pro’s trading capabilities.
• Develop and improve matching engine components, order books, order processing and trade execution workflows. Keep matching deterministic and consistent under peak load, with no crossed books, ghost fills or stale order state.
• Build reliable systems that can handle high transaction volumes while maintaining speed, accuracy and consistency.
• Work on APIs (REST, WebSocket, and later FIX), real-time market data, event-driven services and integrations that connect different parts of the trading platform.
• Improve system performance, reduce latency and identify bottlenecks before they become production issues. Benchmark and profile the matching path, load-test against realistic traffic and measure every change against a baseline.
• Build safeguards that help maintain accurate order processing, transaction integrity and reliable system recovery: pre-trade risk checks, price bands, circuit breakers, kill switches, failover and disaster recovery.
• Keep the ledger exact: trades and fees settled atomically, real-time balances, and crypto and fiat deposits and withdrawals reconciled against custody and banking records.
• Add trading pairs, order types (such as OCO, take-profit and stop-loss) and features, released with zero downtime.
• Analyze business product requirements and propose effective technical solutions.
• Write clean, testable and maintainable code, and participate in code reviews and technical design discussions. Test matching and ledger invariants with simulation and replay.
• Take ownership of features from design and implementation through testing, deployment and ongoing monitoring.
• Share the on-call rotation for production trading systems.
• Collaborate with Product, Engineering and DevOps to deliver key technical priorities.
• Share your knowledge, support other engineers and contribute to strong engineering practices.

What We're Looking For

• 5–7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong backend development experience.
• Strong in Go, or strong in Rust, C++ or Java and willing to work primarily in Go.

• Hands-on experience building, operating or improving trading systems, exchange infrastructure, matching engines or comparable real-time transaction-processing platforms.
• A solid understanding of order books, order lifecycles, matching logic and trade execution.
• Experience building systems where performance, concurrency, reliability and data consistency are critical, including idempotency, exactly-once processing and recovery from partial failures.
• Experience working on systems that require low latency, high availability and predictable execution under heavy load.
• Strong knowledge of data structures, algorithms, databases and distributed systems.
• Experience designing APIs, event-driven services and scalable backend architectures.
• Good judgment in an existing codebase: you improve a live system in small, safe steps rather than reaching for a rewrite.
• Performance work grounded in measurement: profiling, latency percentiles (p99 and above), and memory and garbage-collection tuning.
• Working knowledge of Linux internals (threading, CPU and NUMA effects, system calls) and TCP/UDP networking.
• A practical approach to testing, debugging, performance optimisation and production reliability, including testing that proves correctness through simulation, fuzzing or replaying production traffic.
• You've run what you built in production, including on-call and incident response, and can debug across the OS, network and application layers.
• The ability to take ownership of complex technical work and deliver it with minimal supervision.
• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to communicate technical decisions clearly.

Requirements

• Experience at a cryptocurrency exchange, financial trading platform or electronic market.
• Familiarity with risk controls, settlement or market data infrastructure.
• Crypto infrastructure: wallets, custody, blockchain nodes, deposit and withdrawal pipelines.
• Fiat payment rails: bank transfers, local payment networks, settlement and reconciliation.
• The FIX protocol, event sourcing, or low-latency patterns such as the LMAX Disruptor.
• Experience with market surveillance, regulatory reporting or audits at a regulated venue.
• TypeScript/Node.js for services, gateways or internal tools around the engine.

What Success Looks Like

You'll help us build trading systems that are reliable, performant and ready to scale. You'll take ownership of important engineering deliverables, improve the quality of our infrastructure and help ensure that orders and trades are processed accurately and efficiently.

We value engineers who are proactive, thoughtful in their technical decisions and comfortable taking responsibility for the systems they build.

Why Join Busha?

At Busha, you'll have the opportunity to work on challenging financial technology, influence important engineering decisions and help shape the infrastructure behind Busha Pro.

If you enjoy solving complex backend problems, building performance-sensitive systems and working on technology where reliability and precision genuinely matter, we'd love to hear from you.

Evaluate engagement effectiveness and incremental business impact to continuously optimize strategies.

Drive measurable improvements in user activation, trading conversion, retention, and reactivation.

Project Leadership & Team Management

• Own your services end to end: architecture, implementation, testing, deployment and production behaviour

 - A track record of owning pipelines end to end, making sound technical decisions and improving reliability as requirements and systems evolve.

 - Judgment and autonomy to lead complex work, navigate ambiguity and remain accountable for production outcomes.

 - Experience supporting recurring financial close activities, combined with a proactive approach to identifying manual processes and replacing them with reliable, sustainable automation.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across Engineering and Finance, explain complex technical issues, articulate financial implications, and recommend actionable solutions.

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with cryptocurrency transaction data and how digital-asset activity flows into financial records and reconciliations.

 - Experience processing large volumes of financial transactions using distributed frameworks such as Spark or PySpark.

About the Job

We are looking for a Salesforce QA Engineer who approaches quality with an engineering mindset. At IC, Salesforce is where our sales, retention, partner and support teams work every day, and much of what they see is fetched live from other systems and varies by role, region and regulated entity. You will test custom Lightning Web Components, the automations behind them and the integrations with other systems, planning the edge cases, querying the data and proving what is really happening. If you enjoy writing SOQL to validate complex data, testing APIs with Postman and owning the quality of a feature from refinement to release, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll own

• Collaborate closely with other product streams and technical teams, understand the end-to-end business process, looking beyond the immediate Salesforce implementation to grasp where data originates, how it transforms, and its downstream impact.

• Test features end to end across LWC screens and business logic, from lead conversion and assignment to client lifecycle and partner changes.

• Validate complex CRM processes including client onboarding, automated account assignment, and multi-region regulatory compliance rules.

• Validate end-to-end financial workflows: KYC/verification document pipelines, trading account lifecycle management, and deposit/withdrawal processing.

• Verify bi-directional API data exchange between Salesforce, proprietary services, third-party trading platforms (e.g., MT4/MT5), and payment gateways.

• Test inbound and outbound REST integrations with Postman, covering payloads, status codes, negative cases, simulated errors and integration logs.

• Verify the Salesforce security model by running scenarios as each persona, such as relationship managers, BDMs, partner agents and support staff.

• Design and maintain test plans, test cases and regression suites in Jira and Qmetry.

• Investigate root causes, log high-quality defect reports with detailed reproduction steps, and partner closely with developers through resolution.

• Add acceptance criteria and edge cases in refinement, and run regression in stage and UAT before each release.

• Build and maintain automated UI regression for key user journeys with Playwright.

• Review and refine AI-generated test cases and Playwright scripts against acceptance criteria and designs.

• Propose improvements to our test process, tooling and release checks.

• Own test strategy and release quality as the only QA engineer in your product stream, working alongside the wider Salesforce QA team.

What you’ll need

Essential

Job TitleSenior Platform SRE

Job Description
About IG Group

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here.

Your team
The Platform SRE team is the engine of IG’s reliability programme. We sit within Infrastructure & Operations, working across IG’s hybrid estate of on-premises HashiCorp Nomad and AWS.

We are not a reactive ops team. We build the platform, standards, and tooling that make reliability the default for every engineering team at IG. Through the SRE Guild, we connect with Domain SREs and Reliability Champions across the organisation, setting the bar and lifting it together.

Your role in the Team's Success
You will be a hands-on technical contributor at the heart of the Platform SRE team, owning pieces of the reliability platform that hundreds of engineers depend on. You will work at the intersection of software engineering, observability, and systems reliability, turning reliability from a reactive concern into a proactive engineering discipline.
You will partner with Platform Engineering, product teams, and Reliability Champions to define what good looks like in production and then make it the default. You will contribute to the SRE Guild, mentor engineers across the organisation, and when things go wrong, you will be on the call helping to mitigate, understand, and prevent a repeat.

What you'll do

Build and own the reliability platform
• Implement comprehensive monitoring and observability using OpenTelemetry and distributed tracing. Maintain SLO, error budgets and burn-rate tracking
• Establish and maintain 24/7 operational readiness including automated deployments, blue/green releases, and zero-downtime patching strategies
• Engineer self-healing capabilities: auto-remediation, error-budget-gated rollback, and automated traffic rerouting
• Design and run chaos experiments across the AWS estate, turning severe-but-plausible failure scenarios into engineering improvements
• Build automation tools and CI/CD pipelines that embed reliability practices, while applying software engineering discipline including version control, code reviews, and testing.
• Contribute to the SRE AI agent, IG’s agentic tooling for incident investigation and reliability review, built on AWS frontier models
• Mentor junior SREs and Reliability Champions on reliability patterns and production engineering discipline

Set and uphold standards
• Author and evolve the SRE standards that underpin the Guild: SLO methodology, error budget policy, observability instrumentation guide, and Production Readiness Review (PRR) checklist
• Mentor developers on reliability patterns including circuit breakers, retry logic, and fault tolerance
• Work with development teams and Reliability Champions to design SLOs on customer journeys rather than per-service.
• Assist and guide teams in system design, capacity planning, architectural reviews and closing observability gaps.

Own incident response and learning
• Facilitate blameless post-incident reviews (PIRs) within five working days using contributing-factor methodology
• Maintain the Lessons Register, track remediation actions to closure, and surface patterns across incidents quarterly

What you'll need for this role:

Extensive working experience in all the below mentioned areas.

Essential Technical Skills

• Observability and instrumentation: hands-on OpenTelemetry experience (spans, metrics, traces, context propagation) and production use of Honeycomb, Datadog, Dynatrace, or Grafana; able to instrument Java or Python services directly.
• SLOs and error budgets: proven track record designing customer-meaningful SLIs, setting error budgets, configuring multi-window burn-rate alerts, and working with development teams on reliability measurement
• CI/CD and release engineering: experience building pipelines with safety mechanisms: blue/green and canary releases, automated rollback, and DORA metrics integration
• Container orchestration: Kubernetes (EKS, AKS, or GKE) required; HashiCorp Nomad is a strong advantage on IG’s hybrid estate; solid understanding of cloud networking and IaC (Terraform preferred)
• Software engineering: production-quality coding in Java and/or Python; comfortable contributing to application codebases to implement reliability patterns, not just configuring infrastructure around them
• Distributed systems: strong understanding of how large-scale systems fail and how to make them fail safely; circuit breakers, bulkheads, idempotency, graceful degradation, and load-shedding; high-throughput, low-latency environments preferred
• Incident management: on-call experience on production systems, blameless PIR facilitation, contributing-factor analysis, and driving action items to closure; PagerDuty and ServiceNow familiarity helpful
• Chaos engineering: experience designing and executing hypothesis-driven experiments with blast-radius controls and gap-to-impact-tolerance analysis; AWS FIS, Gremlin, or equivalent
• Community and standards: at ease in a guild or community-of-practice model; comfortable writing RFCs, presenting at engineering forums, and building standards that others will adopt

Experience Requirements
• Track record in high-throughput, production environments (financial services, trading platforms, or similar mission-critical systems preferred)
• Demonstrated ability to improve system reliability and performance at scale
• Experience working collaboratively with development teams to implement observability and reliability improvements
• Strong troubleshooting skills in distributed systems environments

Core Competencies
• Systems thinking approach to problem-solving
• Excellent communication skills for cross-functional collaboration and technical enablement
• Ability to balance hands-on development work with operational responsibilities
• Strong bias toward automation and eliminating manual toil

The Perks

Your growth fuels our success! Thrive with tailored development programs, mentoring opportunities with leaders, and clear career progression. Expand your network through committees, sports and social clubs. Enjoy extra time off for volunteering and community work.

• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total
• The option to buy or sell holiday days.
• Unlimited access to the LinkedIn Learning Platform
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Employee-led LGBTQ+, Women’s, Black and Parents & Carers networks with an annual budget for organising events & projects that foster an open, diverse and inclusive culture
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents
• Option to participate and create ESG initiatives based on IG Brighter Future Fund

 - Speed under pressure. Markets don’t wait for approval cycles and neither do you.

This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.

 




THE OPPORTUNITY

Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will  act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.

 - Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)

 - Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework

 - Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products

 - Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Qualified lawyer admitted in Ireland, England and Wales, or another European Union Member State

 - 15 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, central counterparty or crypto services provider) or at a leading law firm supporting such clients, ideally with in-house or direct product counselling experience

 - Deep, current knowledge of several of the following, with real depth in at least two: MiFID II and MiFIR (investment services, market structure, derivatives and conduct), MiCA (crypto-asset services, custody, trading platforms and stablecoins), European Union payment services and electronic money regulation, and European Union banking regulation

 - Demonstrated ability to analyse novel products against overlapping regimes and give a clear view on classification and perimeter, including in areas where the rules are unsettled or supervisors have not yet spoken

 - Direct experience managing senior regulator relationships, including notifications, information requests, supervisory correspondence and examinations

 - Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including DORA

 - Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions

 - Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing

 - Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders and for senior leadership

 - A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation

 - Experience mentoring or managing lawyers, and the judgement to know when to escalate

Role Overview

This is a hands-on, full-cycle role that owns the whole fraud control loop: investigate, analyze, set up rules, monitor, and improve. You will work tickets daily, turn what you find into data-backed fraud rules and strategies, monitor how they perform, and keep refining them. Each stage feeds the next.

You will own the card risk control strategy, from set-up through ongoing performance, and be accountable for the fraud rate and the interception rate.

Key Responsibilities

1. Investigation

•

Handle card risk tickets daily: review rule-triggered alerts, investigate suspicious accounts and transactions, and decide on block, decline, step-up, or card-lifecycle actions within SLA

•

Investigate fraud typologies: account takeover, card testing, BIN attacks, merchant collusion, friendly fraud, and first-party abuse

•

Assess merchant and transaction risk by MCC risk type, including high-risk merchants and non-card payment flows

•

Manage disputes and chargebacks end to end under Visa/Mastercard rules: evidence, representation, pre-arbitration, and arbitration

2. Data Analysis

•

Turn investigation findings into patterns: analyze ticket, alert, and transaction data to identify fraud trends, attack vectors, and coverage gaps

•

Measure false positives against loss to judge whether existing rules are effective

3. Rule Set-up

•

Design and set up fraud rules, velocity limits, and strategies based on the analysis

•

Make sure rule triggers and decisions stay compliant; escalate linked AML/sanctions concerns to Compliance

4. Rule Monitoring

•

Continuously monitor alert and ticket data after rules go live

•

Track and report KPIs: fraud loss rate (bps), chargeback ratio, approval rate, alert handling time, recovery rate

•

Keep the programme within scheme monitoring thresholds (e.g. VAMP, ECM/EFM) and support scheme and partner audits

5. Rule Improvement

•

Adjust, retire, and add rules in response to monitoring results, balancing fraud loss against false positives and approval rate

•

Feed fraud trends back to Product and Engineering to improve onboarding, 3DS, and authorisation controls

Requirements

•

3+ years in card fraud strategy or payments risk at an issuer, EMI, neobank, PSP, or card programme manager

•

Proven hands-on experience building and tuning fraud rules and strategies, not only working tickets

•

Hands-on knowledge of Visa and/or Mastercard dispute rules, reason codes, and chargeback timelines

•

Experience with MCC-based risk, high-risk merchants, and non-card payments

•

Strong data skills: SQL and Excel/Sheets to pull, slice, and explain fraud trends

•

Fluent English; Mandarin or other European languages are a plus

Nice to Have

•

Crypto-linked or prepaid/debit card programme experience, including crypto-to-fiat conversion at authorisation

•

Card risk control experience across multiple countries/regions

•

Experience launching a card programme in a new market or with a new BIN sponsor

•

Scheme monitoring programme remediation experience

•

Python or BI tooling (Looker, Tableau, Metabase)

•

Certifications: CFE, ACAMS, or equivalent
